stem: A nine-point PPFD map has a good average but much brighter center points and dim corners. What should the technician report?
choices: Report only the average because the mean summarizes overall room intensity and is easiest to compare with target.
Report the mapped distribution and representative grid values, noting the bright center and dim corners rather than hiding them inside the average.
Report only the center values because they show the maximum intensity the canopy receives.
Conclude that the room has a lighting-design defect and recommend fixture changes without further escalation.
rationale: A good average can conceal poor uniformity. If center points are much brighter and corners much dimmer, the distribution is part of the evidence and may matter to crop response. Technician I should preserve the grid pattern and representative values, then escalate interpretation or design decisions that are outside the assigned role.
